content.title: Tide Mill
content.theme: A sea-driven grain mill whose three sluices open and shut on the tide's own count, and a brake that has to be reached before the wheel shakes the mill down.
content.premise: Sedgewick Mill grinds on the ebb: the flood fills the pond behind the sea wall, and the miller lets it out down a race that turns the wheel. Three sluices stand along that race, and none of them is a lever — they run on a count nobody has changed in two hundred years. This ebb the brake pin sheared, the wheel is running free, and the village's grain is inside a building that will not survive it. The brake stands past all three sluices, and the miller's knees will not carry him there.

boundary.message: The tide shoves you back toward the mill yard.
